subject: CareNet request: Availability exhibit + orderform language for enterprise MSA/SOW
content:
From: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@carenet.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carenet.io>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are getting close on procurement and Legal asked that we capture a few commitments in an Availability Exhibit attached to the MSA/SOW and reflected in the order form:

- 99.99% availability (monthly) for inference endpoints that power our clinical decision service (critical path).
- P99 request latency <= 150ms for text-generation endpoints; P95 <= 80ms.
- Maintenance windows limited to a single 2-hour weekly window, with 48-hour advance notice for any rolling upgrades.
- Auditability: 12 months of high-fidelity telemetry and per-tenant event logs that we can reference for SLA breaches.

We understand these are tighter than your standard hosted offering and are open to a commercial trade (committed spend + dedicated capacity) if needed. Please attach your proposed exhibit and order form language and mark up the MSA redlines we sent. We need procurement approval by 2026-11-12 to stay on the timeline.

Attached our MSA redlines and the exhibit template for your review.

Best,
Rachel
Rachel Stern
Head of Procurement, CareNet Health
rachel.stern@carenet.io

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@carenet.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Rachel — thanks for the clear asks and timeline. We appreciate CareNet's clarity on production SLAs. A few quick notes from our side:

- 99.99% is above our standard hosted SLA. We can support that as part of a Dedicated deployment (reserved capacity) with a minimum commit term. I'll outline options: Hosted (standard 99.9%), Dedicated 99.99% (contracted), Private (on-prem/VPC) — by request.
- The latency targets are actionable for inference requests on dedicated pools for models we verify. For hosted, P99 150ms is aggressive for some models/sequence lengths. Need to confirm model+seq distribution.
- Telemetry retention: we can provide 12 months of aggregated token-level billing and request traces; per-tenant raw KV cache traces are sensitive. We can propose an evidence package and a scoped log retention SLA.

I'll attach an initial Availability Exhibit draft and an annotated order-form snippet for CareNet's legal to review. Looping in Monica for the evidence/operational plan and Karthik for contract language.

Next steps: Monica, can you take point on the evidence matrix and write down what we can certify in an order form exhibit vs what requires Dedicated/private? Karthik — can you review the high-level redlines and call out risks (inc. maintenance/force majeure language)?

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com

Attachments: RNW-availability-exhibit-draft.docx, orderform-carenet-commit.json

---

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T08:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Rishi / Karthik — taking this on. Initial thoughts after quick ops sync:

- Dedicated pools: we can realistically commit 99.99% monthly if customer takes a reserved pool sized for peak throughput plus a 20% burst buffer. This requires explicit model pinning and a defined maintenance cadence.
- Latency: P99 150ms is feasible for generator models in 8k context when served on Ampere A100/A10x-class instances with optimized batching and KV caching. For large seq or streaming workloads, we should carve out exceptions in the exhibit.
- Evidence: we will provide per-route SLO dashboards, per-token latency histograms, and a daily breach digest for 12 months. For contractual evidence of breach, our process will rely on telemetry plus incident postmortems.

I drafted a table of what Rhino (our infra team) can provide as 'evidence artifacts' — included in RNW-availability-exhibit-draft.docx. Also adding a suggested credit schedule for any availability breaches (pro-rated credits tied to committed spend).

Action items:
- Karthik: review the credit schedule and maintenance exception language.
- Rishi: propose commercial tier (committed monthly $ / term length) to match 99.99 commitment.
- Rachel: are you able to share expected qps and typical sequence lengths so we can size the dedicated pool recommendation?

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: CareNet_SLA_Redlines_v1.pdf

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Team — quick legal/contract points:

- Avoid unconditional 99.99% for hosted. We should map availability to deployment type in the exhibit and make the order form select the deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private).
- Add language to define what counts as 'Downtime' (control-plane vs data-plane vs scheduled maintenance). We should limit scheduled maintenance to the 2-hour weekly window but allow for emergency fixes with notice & SLA impact mitigation clauses.
- Credits: propose a three-tier credit schedule (monthly availability ranges) capped at X% of monthly committed fees (typical market practice). Define cure period and remediation steps before invoking credits.
- Evidence: require a mutually agreed telemetry dataset and the right to request an audit for breaches — include a process and timeline.

I'll draft redline language around the definitions and credit caps and attach to the RNW-availability-exhibit-draft.docx.

Karthik Iyer
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com

Attachment added: RNW-availability-exhibit-draft.docx (redlines by Legal)

---

From: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@carenet.io>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@carenet.io>
Date: 2026-11-04T14:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Rishi — thanks for the quick turnaround and draft. A few clarifications from CareNet Legal / Eng: 

- CareNet is prepared to commit to a 12-month minimum and to a $200k/mo committed spend for a dedicated pool if that enables 99.99% availability and the latency SLOs.
- For sizing: typical sustained QPS for the clinical endpoint is ~120 req/s with average sequence length ~900 tokens; bursts up to 350 req/s during batch processing windows.
- Evidence: CareNet requires per-tenant traceability to tie a specific incident to our workload (not just region-level aggregates). If raw traces are sensitive, we can accept signed attestations + incident timelines.

Please confirm whether the committed spend + dedicated pool would satisfy the 99.99 and latency targets, and share the edited exhibit and order form language so our procurement can close by 2026-11-12.

Regards,
Rachel

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Stern <rachel.stern@carenet.io>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Daniel Cho <daniel@carenet.io>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Requesting availability exhibit + orderform language for MSA/SOW attachments

Rachel / Daniel — good to see the committed spend number and traffic profile; that helps a lot. Short answer: yes, the committed $200k/mo + dedicated reserved pool can be sized to provide a contractual 99.99% monthly availability and meet the latency SLOs for the stated profile, provided we agree on:

1) Model pinning: CareNet should pin the production model versions in the order form exhibit to avoid performance regressions from model swaps.
2) Maintenance policy: 2-hr weekly window formalized in the exhibit; emergency maintenance limited with customer notice and targeted mitigation.
3) Evidence & audit: we will provide per-route latency/availability dashboards and a breach packet (telemetry export + incident postmortem). For regulatory audits, we'll accept a joint-attestation process or a scoped SOC2 supplement.

Next steps:
- Karthik: please finalize credit schedule and MSA redline.
- Monica: finalize the evidence matrix and confirm telemetry extracts we can safely deliver (and any redaction needs).
- Rachel / Daniel: if you can sign the attached order form (DocuSign link below) we will schedule a capacity planning call with Infra and Solutions on 2026-11-09 to finalize pool sizing.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example/ABC123
HubSpot: HS-897621

Rishi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
